chunks: From him, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, who said:

I said to Zurarah: 'Indeed, some people have narrated to me from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon them) about various matters regarding inheritance, so I will present them to you. Whatever of them is false, say

key_terms.أَبُو جَعْفَر: Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (peace be upon him)
key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّ: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
key_terms.زُرَارَة: Zurarah ibn A'yan, a prominent Imamite scholar
key_terms.مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ مُسْلِم: Muhammad ibn Muslim, a companion of the Imams

ai.seo_question: What did Zurarah say about the inheritance of the husband and parents according to the Imams?
ai.summary: This hadith highlights Zurarah’s role as a primary authority in Shia jurisprudence, validating the inheritance distribution for spouses and parents as reported from the Imams. It underscores the methodological rigor of the early scholars in verifying narrations against the teachings of Imam al-Baqir and Imam al-Sadiq, ensuring the authenticity of legal rulings in the chapter of *Fara'id*. The confirmation of this specific narration reinforces the Shia interpretation of Quranic verses regarding the residual shares of parents when spouses are present.
